jobs.description: ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD. At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career. THE ROLE: We are seeking a Strategic Sourcing Manager to lead cable-related sourcing and supply management activities for server and rack system solutions. This position will partner with cable suppliers, engineering teams, procurement, and other cross-functional stakeholders to manage sourcing activities throughout the product design and development lifecycle. The Strategic Sourcing Manager will be responsible for supplier quotations and negotiations, costed BOM management, NPI development costs, material readiness, forecast and demand execution, and supply-chain risk mitigation. THE PERSON: The ideal candidate is a proactive, detail-oriented sourcing and supply-chain professional with experience supporting cable products used in server and rack systems. You have a strong understanding of BOM structures, product design milestones, NPI processes, supplier management, procurement principles, and material planning. You can manage multiple priorities, analyze complex information, maintain accurate trackers, and communicate effectively with suppliers, engineers, and cross-functional stakeholders. You take ownership of issues, act with urgency, and follow actions through resolution. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Conduct RFQs with cable suppliers for costed BOMs, NPI development expenses, tooling or other applicable nonrecurring costs, and engineering change requirements at each product design milestone. Evaluate supplier quotations and negotiate pricing, development costs, change-related expenses, material commitments, and delivery schedules. Develop and maintain effective working relationships with cable suppliers to support sourcing, product development, and supply continuity objectives. Track and manage cable-related BOMs, part numbers, supplier information, costs, and change histories throughout each milestone of the product design lifecycle. Partner with engineering teams and cable suppliers to understand design requirements, identify sourcing dependencies, and support the timely execution of NPI activities. Monitor raw-material readiness with suppliers and maintain clear, well-structured trackers for material status, shortages, risks, actions, owners, and recovery dates. Identify, track, and report critical material shortages and coordinate with suppliers and cross-functional teams to expedite raw materials and improve delivery schedules. Release cable-related forecasts and demand orders to suppliers and negotiate supply commitments to support required production and material delivery schedules. Work with suppliers, engineers, procurement, and supply-chain teams to develop and execute material-readiness and supply-risk mitigation plans. Proactively identify potential continuity, capacity, lead-time, quality, cost, and delivery risks and drive corrective actions through resolution. Manage material readiness in a manner that supports supply continuity while reducing excess and obsolete inventory exposure. Use analytical tools and supply-chain data to evaluate forecasts, demand requirements, supplier performance, material readiness, and sourcing risks. Communicate status, priorities, issues, and recommended actions clearly and accurately to suppliers and internal stakeholders. Demonstrate strong planning and organizational skills by maintaining accurate sourcing and material-readiness trackers. Manage multiple projects and competing priorities in a fast-paced product development and supply-chain environment. Take accountability for assigned actions and proactively drive issues to timely resolution. Collaborate effectively across organizations to achieve sourcing, supply-chain, and company objectives. Maintain a strong focus on results, information accuracy, and attention to detail PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, supply planning, supplier management, or a related supply-chain function. Industry experience within ODM/OEM manufacturing, server system solutions, rack-level infrastructure, electronics, cables, or a related technology manufacturing environment. Experience managing supplier RFQs, costed BOMs, NPI development expenses, forecasts, purchase or demand releases, and delivery commitments. Knowledge of cable products, BOM structures, part number management, product design processes, and engineering change activities for server or rack systems. Experience monitoring supplier material readiness, identifying material shortages, expediting deliveries, and developing supply-risk mitigation plans. Understanding of excess and obsolete inventory risk and the relationship between forecasts, demand changes, supplier commitments, and material procurement. Advanced analytical, problem-solving, communication, negotiation, multitasking, and prioritization skills. Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel and PowerPoint. Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including experience analyzing data using PivotTables, VLOOKUP or comparable lookup functions, formulas, filters, and structured trackers. Demonstrated ability to work effectively with suppliers, engineers, procurement professionals, operations teams, and other cross-functional stakeholders. Proficiency in procurement and supply-chain principles and practices. Professional proficiency in English; bilingual proficiency in Mandarin is preferred. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Industrial Administration, Technology Administration, Supply Chain Management, Engineering, or a related field LOCATION: AMD Secaucus, New Jersey This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. #LI-AJ1 Benefits offered are described: AMD benefits at a glance . We encourage applications from all qualified candidates and will accommodate applicants’ needs under the respective laws throughout all stages of the recruitment and selection process. 직무 소개
Digital Trust PMO 조직 내 Business Controlling & Analytics 핵심 팀원으로서 조직 운영 전반에 대한 예산, 구매, 계약, 인력 및 운영 데이터를 관리하고 지원하는 역할입니다. 본 포지션은 단순한 데이터 분석가(Data Analyst)가 아닌, PMO 관점에서 조직 운영을 지원하고 관리할 수 있는 Business Operations 및 Operational Management 전문가를 채용하기 위한 포지션입니다.
주요 업무는 연간 예산 계획(AOP) 수립 지원, 분기별 Forecast 및 Actual 관리, 구매 및 계약 운영, Vendor 및 Invoice 관리, Headcount 및 채용 현황 관리, Executive Reporting 지원 등으로 구성되며, 조직 운영 전반이 원활하게 수행될 수 있도록 다양한 운영 프로세스를 관리하고 지원하는 핵심 역할을 담당합니다.
또한 PMO Manager 및 조직 리더들과 긴밀히 협업하며 예산, 인력, 구매, 계약 및 운영 현황에 대한 가시성을 제공하고, 조직의 의사결정을 지원하기 위한 운영 데이터 및 리포트를 제공하게 됩니다.
본 역할은 빠르게 변화하는 환경에서 다수의 업무를 동시에 관리하고, 변화하는 비즈니스 우선순위에 유연하게 대응할 수 있는 높은 수준의 실행력, 꼼꼼함, Ownership 및 Stakeholder Management 역량을 요구합니다.
특히 다양한 글로벌 이해관계자와 직접 협업하는 역할인 만큼, 한국어와 영어를 활용하여 통역 없이 원활하게 커뮤니케이션할 수 있는 역량이 필수적입니다.
본 포지션은 Power BI 또는 Tableau 중심의 순수 Data Analytics 역할이 아니며, PMO 운영, 예산 관리, 구매 및 계약 운영, 인력 관리, Executive Reporting 등 조직 운영 전반을 지원하고 관리하는 Business Operations 중심의 역할입니다.본 포지션은 대규모 조직의 운영을 지원하는 역할로, 여러 업무를 동시에 처리하고 다양한 이해관계자와 협업하며 높은 수준의 정확성과 실행력을 유지할 수 있는 분을 찾고 있습니다.

jobs.description: About Us Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid. At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world. Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you. Job Description Software Development Engineers are expert problem-solvers and builders who design, implement, and improve software applications and systems. In this role, engineers spend approximately 60–75% of their time coding, working hands-on with code, data, and modern tools (including AI-assisted development, cloud services, and automation frameworks) to deliver secure, scalable, and high-quality technology solutions that drive business outcomes in the fintech sector. They collaborate with cross-functional teams – product managers, designers, data scientists, QA, operations, and compliance – to translate business requirements into robust technical solutions, all while adhering to best practices, security standards, and regulatory requirements. All roles require digital fluency, including the ability to work with emerging technologies such as Generative AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot) to support everyday work. Key Responsibilities: Collaborate with stakeholders to interpret requirements for project components and incorporate feedback into future designs or solution fixes. Translate business requirements by verifying assumptions and escalating potential design issues to appropriate stakeholders. Assist in identifying risks in solutions and communicate impacts to senior engineers. Design and develop product components based on needs/requests of more senior engineers, contributing to design documentation and validating alignment with requirements. Participate in project estimation and escalate issues that may cause delays. Create and implement code for products, services, or components that are extensible and maintainable, applying coding patterns, guidelines, and best practices. Apply security assessment processes to ensure code is free from threats or risks. Use debugging tools to verify assumptions and proactively flag issues before they occur. Participate in code reviews to ensure coding standards are followed and address routine pull requests. Create test plans and configure testing procedures to identify and resolve defects for multiple features. Respond to incidents during on-call rotations, troubleshooting issues and deploying fixes under appropriate guidance. Leverage and build knowledge of software developer tools to create, debug, and maintain code for components. Remain current in skills by investing time in training resources to improve product availability, reliability, efficiency, observability, and performance. Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager. Qualifications Basic Qualifications: 2+ years of relevant work experience and a Bachelors degree, OR 5+ years of relevant work experience Preferred Qualifications: 3 or more years of work experience with a Bachelor’s Degree or more than 2 years of work experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, MD) Experience in technologies/software systems or a directly related field (minimum two years). Experience in developing and/or implementing web-based or mobile applications (minimum two years). Experience in Math, Science, Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, or related field (Master’s or Bachelor’s degree required). Experience in creating and implementing code for products, services, or components. Experience in applying coding patterns, guidelines, and best practices. Lead technical discovery workshops, client design sessions, architecture reviews and solution walkthroughs with issuers, processors, technology partners and internal stakeholders. Identify strategic opportunities through client engagement, market research, competitive analysis and industry developments. Evaluate product initiatives and investment opportunities based on client value, commercial potential, technical feasibility, implementation complexity, scalability and strategic alignment. Experience working with multi-currency, wallet, FX or banking platforms such as Currencycloud is highly desirable. 5-8+ years of experience in product management, technical product management, payments, FX, multicurrency solutions, issuer processing or cross-border payments. About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
Anthropic's Application Security team secures the systems that build, serve, and increasingly
are
Claude — and as Anthropic's footprint grows, that mandate now extends to companies and codebases we bring in from outside. This role establishes that function.
You'll own security due diligence and secure integration for Anthropic's acquisitions — assessing a target's security posture pre-close, writing the security risk readout for leadership, and after close, bringing acquired systems up to Anthropic's bar. Security has been part of every deal to date, but this is the first dedicated role for it: you'll formalize the playbook, the risk model, and the tooling, and make them repeatable.
This is an AppSec role first. You'll be an active member of the Application Security team — same rituals, same on-run rotation, same tooling, working alongside engineers securing Anthropic's own agentic product surfaces. The expectation is the same too: we use Claude as our primary tool, and you're expected to automate the repeatable parts of diligence and integration as you go, so each acquisition is easier than the last. When deal flow is quiet, you'll pick up core AppSec project work; when it's active, M&A is your priority.
We're upfront that the center of gravity here is M&A rather than core product security. It's burstier, more assessment-heavy, and operates on confidential, time-sensitive work. If you like parachuting into an unfamiliar codebase under time pressure and turning it into a clear risk picture for leadership, this is that job.
Key responsibilities
Lead pre-close security due diligence on prospective acquisitions — coordinate external penetration testing, threat-model the target's architecture, assess security controls, and deliver the security risk readout for leadership ahead of close and integration planning
Drive post-close security integration — stand up static and dynamic analysis coverage on acquired codebases, track high- and critical-severity remediation to closure, fold acquired assets into bug bounty scope, and onboard repositories to Anthropic's automated vulnerability remediation and reporting systems
Coordinate adjacent security engineering teams (supply chain, cloud, corporate security, detection & response) on their portions of each integration
Work across a wide set of stakeholders on every deal — corporate development, legal, security leadership, and the engineering teams inheriting acquired systems internally; engineering and security counterparts at the target company externally — translating between them and keeping the security workstream legible to all of them
Formalize and scale Anthropic's M&A security playbook — risk-scoring model, diligence runbook, integration checklist — and turn as much of it as possible into Claude-powered tooling rather than manual process
Share the team's operational on-run rotation (bug bounty escalations, launch consults, incident response), swapping out during periods of active deal work
Contribute to core AppSec projects between deals — secure design reviews, threat modeling for agentic systems, and the team's security automation roadmap
Minimum qualifications
Hands-on application and infrastructure security experience, including cloud and containerized environments
Demonstrated ability to rapidly assess an unfamiliar codebase or architecture and produce a clear, prioritized risk assessment for a non-security audience
Production-quality coding ability in at least one of Python, Go, Rust, or TypeScript
Practical threat-modeling and vulnerability-identification skills — you've found and reasoned about real bugs in real systems
Comfort operating with high autonomy, ambiguity, and tightly-held confidential context
Clear written and verbal communication across varied audiences — executives, legal and corporate development partners, and engineering counterparts at an acquired company
Preferred qualifications
7+ years in application security, security consulting, or security architecture
Prior M&A security due diligence, third-party security assessment, or technical due diligence experience
Experience standing up or scaling SAST/DAST, bug bounty, or vulnerability management coverage across multiple codebases
Track record of building security automation or tooling rather than relying solely on manual review
Familiarity with using LLMs as a core part of your security workflow
Experience securing agentic, code-execution, or LLM-integrated systems
Representative projects
Point Anthropic's internal LLM-driven code analysis and AI-assisted scanning at an acquired repository nobody here has seen, and turn the output into a prioritized remediation plan in days rather than weeks
Design the risk-scoring framework Anthropic uses to compare security posture across acquisitions of different shapes and sizes
Build the automation that onboards an acquired codebase to Anthropic's vulnerability dashboard, dependency auto-patching, and bounty scope without a human running a checklist
Write the security risk memo for a live deal and present it to corporate development and security leadership
